rows.selection_reason: With no completed experiments, the main uncertainty is whether a simple RNA-only baseline provides a useful performance reference for the study. This configuration tests the simplest RNA representation and profile setting, PCA with a single profile, without adding aggregation, image features, or fusion complexity. It is the best first experiment because it establishes a low-cost anchor for later comparisons of RNA encoders, multiprofile aggregation, image-only models, and multimodal fusion.

Only the RNA-only single-profile PCA baseline is known (acc 0.485, F1 0.464), so it is unclear whether image features are predictive at all. config_010 tests the minimal image-only counterpart using ResNet50 and singleprofile, isolating the modality/representation question without introducing aggregation or fusion. Establishing an image-only baseline is essential before spending budget on multimodal fusion or more complex multiprofile settings, because it clarifies whether image can contribute and provides a reference for later encoder and fusion comparisons.

RNA-only PCA single-profile is much stronger than image-only ResNet, so the next experiment should exploit the more promising RNA branch. config_002 keeps the same PCA encoder and tests whether adding multiple profiles with simple avgpool aggregation improves over the single-profile baseline. This isolates the effect of profile setting/aggregation and clarifies whether RNA representation complexity is worthwhile before testing new encoders or fusion.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile RNA with avgpool and PCA (config_002, accuracy 0.591, F1 0.573) clearly outperforms singleprofile PCA RNA (config_001, accuracy 0.485, F1 0.464), while image-only ResNet is weak (config_010, accuracy 0.208). The key uncertainty is whether the multiprofile gain is already captured by simple average pooling or whether transformer aggregation would further improve the representation. config_003 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping rna_only, multiprofile, and pca_n2000 fixed, so it cleanly isolates the aggregation effect. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the strongest current direction with a low-confound comparison and provides high-leverage information for choosing aggregation in later multimodal settings.

RNA-only multiprofile with avgpool and PCA is the current best setting (0.591 accuracy / 0.573 F1), and avgpool clearly outperforms transformer aggregation for multiprofile RNA. The key remaining uncertainty is whether a learned RNA representation can improve over PCA in this promising profile/aggregation setting. config_005 changes only the RNA encoder to scvi_n200, isolating the effect of representation while exploiting the best known RNA design. This is an efficient next step because it has strong expected performance and will determine whether future multimodal models should build on PCA or a learned RNA encoder.

RNA-only multiprofile scvi_n200 with avgpool is the current best configuration (0.650 accuracy, 0.628 F1), while image-only ResNet50 is weak (0.208 accuracy). The key uncertainty is whether image features provide complementary signal to the strong RNA pipeline. config_030 keeps the best RNA encoder, multiprofile setting, and avgpool aggregation, adds ResNet50, and uses a simple concat fusion, directly testing the value of multimodal fusion with minimal added complexity. If it improves over the RNA-only baseline, multimodal modeling is promising; if not, it supports focusing on RNA-only designs.

The strongest evidence is that RNA-only with scvi_n200, multiprofile, and avgpool is the best configuration so far (0.650 accuracy), and the only multimodal test with the same RNA settings plus resnet50 and concat fusion is slightly lower (0.632 accuracy). This leaves uncertainty about whether the small multimodal drop is due to concat fusion or the image encoder itself. config_031 changes only fusion from concat to weighted while keeping scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool, and resnet50 fixed, so it isolates the fusion effect. It is the best next experiment because it directly tests whether the promising scvi/multiprofile/avgpool direction can be made multimodal with a better fusion rule before spending limited budget on less-supported image encoders or aggregation changes.

The current best result is config_031 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) with validation accuracy 0.678 and F1 0.646, showing that weighted fusion and scvi + avgpool are promising. The key remaining uncertainty in this strong direction is whether transformer aggregation can improve over avgpool for scvi; transformer was worse for pca, but that has not been tested with scvi or weighted multimodal fusion. config_033 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer relative to config_031, cleanly isolating the aggregation effect. This is an efficient next experiment because it directly extends the best-performing setup and clarifies whether to invest further in transformer aggregation or continue exploiting avgpool.

The strongest evidence is for multimodal multiprofile scvi + resnet50, where weighted fusion beats concat under avgpool and transformer aggregation further improves performance under weighted fusion. However, it is unclear whether the gain from config_031 to config_033 is driven mainly by transformer aggregation, weighted fusion, or their interaction. config_032 keeps the same RNA encoder, image encoder, profile setting, and aggregation as the current best config_033 but changes only fusion from weighted to concat. This completes the fusion-by-aggregation comparison, directly tests whether transformer aggregation helps even with concat, and clarifies whether weighted fusion is necessary. It is a single-factor, low-risk extension of the most promising direction and is more informative than immediately testing a new image encoder while the aggregation/fusion interaction remains unresolved.

RNA-only scvi avgpool is already strong (0.650), and the best multimodal setup uses transformer aggregation (0.713), but it is unclear whether transformer aggregation helps the RNA branch itself or only when combined with image/fusion. config_006 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer in the best RNA-only scvi multiprofile setting, isolating the aggregation effect. This reduces uncertainty about whether a simpler RNA-only model can match the multimodal gain and whether future budget should focus on RNA aggregation/encoder or image fusion.
